# Risk Management Plan Template

## 1. Executive Summary

### 1.1 Purpose
This Risk Management Plan defines how risks will be identified, analyzed, and managed throughout the project lifecycle.

### 1.2 Scope
This plan covers all project-related risks including:
- Technical risks
- Business risks
- Operational risks
- External risks
- Resource risks

### 1.3 Risk Management Objectives
- Minimize the probability and impact of negative risks
- Maximize the probability and impact of positive risks (opportunities)
- Provide systematic approach to risk management
- Enable proactive risk response

## 2. Risk Management Methodology

### 2.1 Risk Management Process
1. **Risk Identification** - Identify potential risks
2. **Risk Analysis** - Assess probability and impact
3. **Risk Response Planning** - Develop response strategies
4. **Risk Monitoring** - Track risks and responses
5. **Risk Control** - Implement risk responses

### 2.2 Risk Categories
| Category | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Technical | Technology-related risks | System failures, integration issues |
| Business | Business environment risks | Market changes, competition |
| Operational | Day-to-day operation risks | Resource availability, process issues |
| External | Outside project control | Regulatory changes, vendor issues |
| Resource | People and equipment risks | Key person departure, equipment failure |

### 2.3 Risk Identification Techniques
- Brainstorming sessions
- Expert interviews
- Historical data analysis
- Checklist reviews
- SWOT analysis
- Root cause analysis

## 3. Risk Assessment Framework

### 3.1 Probability Scale
| Level | Description | Probability Range |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| Very High | Almost certain to occur | 81-100% |
| High | Likely to occur | 61-80% |
| Medium | May occur | 41-60% |
| Low | Unlikely to occur | 21-40% |
| Very Low | Rare, but possible | 1-20% |

### 3.2 Impact Scale
| Level | Cost Impact | Schedule Impact | Quality Impact | Scope Impact |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|--------------|
| Very High | >20% increase | >20% delay | Major degradation | Major scope reduction |
| High | 10-20% increase | 10-20% delay | Significant degradation | Significant scope reduction |
| Medium | 5-10% increase | 5-10% delay | Moderate degradation | Moderate scope reduction |
| Low | 1-5% increase | 1-5% delay | Minor degradation | Minor scope reduction |
| Very Low | <1% increase | <1% delay | Negligible impact | Negligible impact |

### 3.3 Risk Scoring Matrix
| Probability \ Impact | Very Low | Low | Medium | High | Very High |
|---------------------|----------|-----|--------|------|-----------|
| **Very High** | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 | 25 |
| **High** | 4 | 8 | 12 | 16 | 20 |
| **Medium** | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 15 |
| **Low** | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |
| **Very Low** | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |

### 3.4 Risk Priority Levels
- **Critical (20-25)**: Immediate attention required
- **High (15-19)**: Senior management attention
- **Medium (8-14)**: Management attention
- **Low (4-7)**: Monitor and manage
- **Very Low (1-3)**: Accept and monitor

## 4. Risk Response Strategies

### 4.1 Negative Risk (Threat) Responses
- **Avoid**: Eliminate the risk by changing the project plan
- **Mitigate**: Reduce probability or impact
- **Transfer**: Shift risk to third party (insurance, contracts)
- **Accept**: Acknowledge risk and take no action

### 4.2 Positive Risk (Opportunity) Responses
- **Exploit**: Ensure the opportunity is realized
- **Enhance**: Increase probability or positive impact
- **Share**: Allocate ownership to third party best able to capture opportunity
- **Accept**: Take advantage if opportunity occurs

### 4.3 Response Planning Criteria
| Risk Level | Response Required | Timeline | Authority |
|------------|-------------------|----------|-----------|
| Critical | Mandatory response plan | Immediate | Project Sponsor |
| High | Detailed response plan | Within 1 week | Project Manager |
| Medium | Basic response plan | Within 2 weeks | Risk Owner |
| Low | Monitor only | As needed | Risk Owner |
| Very Low | Document only | As needed | Risk Owner |

## 5. Risk Register Template

### 5.1 Risk Register Fields
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Risk ID | Unique identifier |
| Risk Description | Clear description of the risk |
| Risk Category | Category from defined list |
| Probability | Likelihood of occurrence |
| Impact | Consequence if occurs |
| Risk Score | Probability × Impact |
| Risk Priority | Critical/High/Medium/Low/Very Low |
| Risk Owner | Person responsible for managing |
| Response Strategy | Avoid/Mitigate/Transfer/Accept |
| Response Actions | Specific actions to be taken |
| Target Date | When response should be completed |
| Status | Open/In Progress/Closed |
| Residual Risk | Risk remaining after response |

## 6. Roles and Responsibilities

### 6.1 Risk Management Team
| Role | Responsibilities |
|------|------------------|
| **Project Sponsor** | - Approve risk management plan<br>- Provide resources for risk responses<br>- Make go/no-go decisions |
| **Project Manager** | - Overall risk management accountability<br>- Lead risk identification and planning<br>- Report risks to stakeholders |
| **Risk Manager** | - Facilitate risk management process<br>- Maintain risk register<br>- Monitor risk responses |
| **Risk Owners** | - Monitor assigned risks<br>- Implement risk responses<br>- Report status updates |
| **Team Members** | - Identify risks in their areas<br>- Support risk assessment<br>- Execute risk responses |

## 7. Risk Monitoring and Control

### 7.1 Risk Review Schedule
- **Daily**: Risk owner monitoring
- **Weekly**: Team risk review
- **Bi-weekly**: Risk register update
- **Monthly**: Stakeholder risk report
- **Phase Gates**: Comprehensive risk review

### 7.2 Risk Reporting
| Report Type | Audience | Frequency | Content |
|-------------|----------|-----------|---------|
| Risk Dashboard | Project Team | Weekly | Top risks, trends, actions |
| Risk Status | Stakeholders | Monthly | Risk summary, changes, issues |
| Risk Report | Sponsor/Board | Quarterly | Comprehensive analysis |

### 7.3 Risk Metrics
- Number of risks by category
- Number of risks by priority level
- Risk closure rate
- Risk response effectiveness
- New risks identified per period

## 8. Risk Communication Plan

### 8.1 Communication Matrix
| Stakeholder | Information Needs | Method | Frequency | Owner |
|-------------|-------------------|--------|-----------|-------|
| Project Team | All risks, detailed status | Risk register, meetings | Weekly | Risk Manager |
| Project Sponsor | High/critical risks | Dashboard, reports | Bi-weekly | Project Manager |
| Steering Committee | Top risks, trends | Executive summary | Monthly | Project Manager |

### 8.2 Risk Communication Guidelines
- **Transparency**: All risks should be openly communicated
- **Timeliness**: New risks communicated within 24 hours
- **Clarity**: Use plain language, avoid jargon
- **Actionable**: Include specific actions and timelines

## When to Use

Use throughout the project lifecycle to identify, assess, and track risks. This template is essential for projects with significant complexity, multiple stakeholders, or high business impact, where structured risk management provides decision-making value.

## When NOT to Use

Do not use for very low-risk, short-duration tasks where informal risk awareness is sufficient. Avoid this template if your governance framework requires a different risk management approach or if stakeholders prefer real-time risk dashboards over static registers.
